L3 · Brand colors

Seven ways to wear red

Same system in every option: your hand logo as the profile picture, the same nine posts, and an LED title card. Each one has its own colors and its own font. Photos are toned to match.

Pick one for tomorrow

Text Jonathan the number. That color and font go on everything we make for the studio: the LED title cards, the loops and the covers. You can also mix, like the colors from one and the font from another.

Jonathan's pick

5 · Red · Cream

Red, white and black are Coca-Cola's own colors. Shooting at Coke Studio in those, you read as part of their branding instead of your own. Cream breaks that, its warmth matches the old-film horror look on ThrizzL3, and the gothic blackletter fits both the horror and LA street style.

  • Grey options read flat on a phone and pull away from the party energy.
  • Black still shows up in your photos and shadows. It just isn't a brand color.

What this changes

Whichever you pick sets the colors for everything else: the profile picture, cover templates, title cards, and the LED loops. The black-and-white horror loops stay black and white, with your pick as the accent.
